Now I have the complete picture. Here's the report.

## Report: CLI vs Web Tool Rendering Gap

### 1. CLI tool-call rendering today
- **Entry point**: `/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/src/cli/main.ts` — `keating shell` calls `launchShell(cwd, args)` (line 453).
- **Runtime**: `/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/src/runtime/pi.ts:312-382` — `launchShell` `spawn()`s an **external binary**, `pi` (package `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`), with `stdio: "inherit"`. Keating hands the terminal entirely to that external process; there is no ink/blessed TUI loop inside this repo for the chat itself.
- **Tool definitions**: `/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/src/pi/hyperteacher-extension.ts` (1363 lines) registers Keating's tools (`plan`, `map`, `animate`, `verify`, `quiz`, `bench`, `ask_user_question`, `keating_voice`, etc.) onto the `pi` runtime via `pi.registerTool(...)`. Every tool just returns `{ content: [{ type: "text", text }] }` — plain markdown/text (e.g. quiz at line 732-746 returns `quizToMarkdown` + answer key as one string). Only `ask_user_question` (line 959-1004) embeds a machine-readable tag: `<keating-question json=${JSON.stringify(payload)} />` (single-JSON, not double-encoded) — but since the CLI has no parser for it, it's just printed as literal text by `pi`'s own renderer.
- **Ink usage**: only in `/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/src/cli/setup.ts` (imports `Box, Text, render, useApp, useInput` from `ink`) for the one-time interactive setup wizard — not used for chat/tool rendering.
- **Plain ANSI helpers**: `/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/src/core/terminal.ts` — `printInfo/printSuccess/printWarning/printError/printSection/printPanel/printAsciiHeader`, raw `\x1b[...]` true-color codes matching the web palette 1:1 (comment at line 15). No box-drawing for structured data beyond `printPanel`, no tables, no progress meters.

### 2. Web interactive-card pattern
- **Web tool defs** (separate implementation from CLI's): `/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/browser-tools.ts`, e.g. quiz at line ~1143: `` `[artifact://plan/${saved.id}]\n\n${md}\n---\n${answers}\n\n<keating-quiz json=${JSON.stringify(JSON.stringify(quiz))} />` `` — the **double-JSON encoding** (`JSON.stringify` applied twice).
- **Parser/dispatcher**: `/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/components/AssistantChatPanel.tsx` — `parseInteractiveSegments` (~line 1078) regex-matches tags `<keating-quiz>`, `<keating-scene>`, `<keating-question>`, `<keating-goal>`, `<keating-quiz-result>`, `<keating-quiz-grade>` (patterns at lines 1066-1068+). Payloads are recovered with `JSON.parse(JSON.parse(seg.json))` (lines 1226, 1247, 1272, 1309, 1330, 1341, 1360).
- **Result wiring**: on user interaction, components `window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("keating:question-answered" / "keating:quiz-submitted" / etc.))`; `AssistantChatPanel`'s `onNew` callback (defined ~line 2753) listens via `window.addEventListener(...)` (lines 2855-2971) and feeds the answer back into the agent conversation as a new message.
- **Card components**: `/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/components/QuizRenderer.tsx`, `QuizResultCard.tsx`, `QuizSessionPanel.tsx`, `GoalRenderer.tsx`, plus `quiz-grades-context.ts` and `animation-host.ts` (for `<keating-scene>`).

### 3. Rich-web / plain-CLI tools
`quiz` (interactive `QuizRenderer` card in web vs. flat markdown Q&A dump in CLI), `ask_user_question` (interactive form UI in web vs. plain question text in CLI, and CLI's tag isn't even parsed), `goal` (`GoalRenderer.tsx` vs. no CLI equivalent found), `map`/`animate`/`plan`/`verify` (CLI just writes files and prints a path — `[artifact://map]` etc. — with no visual rendering at all in either surface beyond web's `ArtifactViewer.tsx`, per memory `PlanViewer` was removed for quiz).

### 4/5. Gap summary
CLI has: ANSI color/box helpers (`terminal.ts`) and one ink-based wizard (`setup.ts`) — enough scaffolding to build boxes/colors, but **no tag parser, no interactive prompt loop, and no ownership of the chat rendering surface** (that's the external `pi` binary via `stdio: inherit`). To add CLI card rendering you'd need either: (a) get `pi` to expose a tool-output hook/plugin point, or (b) intercept/wrap its stdio, or (c) add an ink-based interactive-prompt fallback purely for `ask_user_question`-style blocking tools. Tool schemas are **not shared** — CLI (`src/pi/hyperteacher-extension.ts`) and web (`web/src/keating/browser-tools.ts`) each define their own tool sets independently; `shared/` (per memory `project_shared_code_cross_package.md`) only contains `finetune-parse.ts` and import logic, not tool/tag schemas.

## Findings

**1. `pi` is a full TS library with types, not a black box.**
Installed at `/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` (v0.80.2, resolved via bun store `.bun/@earendil-works+pi-coding-agent@0.80.2+.../`). `package.json` declares `"main": "./dist/index.js"`, `"types": "./dist/index.d.ts"`. Extension/tool types live in `node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts`. It depends on sibling packages `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core` (tool/result types) and `@earendil-works/pi-tui` (TUI primitives, `Component`, `TUI`, `OverlayHandle`).

**2. Tool result shape supports structured details + custom render, not just plain text.**
`AgentToolResult<T>` (`.../pi-agent-core/dist/types.d.ts:306-316`):
```ts
export interface AgentToolResult<T> {
  content: (TextContent | ImageContent)[];  // sent back to the model
  details: T;                                // arbitrary structured data for UI rendering
  terminate?: boolean;
}
```
Crucially, `types.d.ts:800` and `:865` in the extension API expose `registerMessageRenderer<T>(customType: string, renderer: MessageRenderer<T>)` where `MessageRenderer<T> = (message: CustomMessage<T>, options, theme) => Component | undefined` (`extensions/types.d.ts:800,864-867`), plus `sendMessage(...)` to emit a `CustomMessage`. This is exactly a plugin rendering hook: an extension can register a custom `Component` renderer keyed by `customType`, and later send messages of that type that pi's TUI renders with the custom component instead of plain markdown/text. `details` on `AgentToolResult` is explicitly documented as "for logs or UI rendering," implying tool results can carry rich structured data consumed by such a renderer.

**3. pi already has built-in interactive-prompt UI primitives — and Keating already uses them.**
`ExtensionContext.ui` (`extensions/types.d.ts` ~44-136) exposes `select(title, labels)`, `input(title, prefill)`, `confirm(title, summary)`, `notify(message, level)`, `setEditorText`, `setWidget`, `setHeader`, `editor(title, prefill)`, plus `addAutocompleteProvider`. Keating's own `/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/src/pi/hyperteacher-extension.ts` already calls these extensively: `ctx.ui.select(...)` (lines 255, 1170, 1271), `ctx.ui.input(...)` (line 263), `ctx.ui.confirm(...)` (line 329), `ctx.ui.setEditorText(...)` (many lines), `ctx.ui.setWidget`/`setHeader` (lines 1346-1349). So mid-execution interactive prompts are a first-class, already-used pi API — no need to build a separate prompt mechanism.

Important correction to the premise: this extension code runs *inside the `pi` process* (loaded via `--extension <path>` at `src/runtime/pi.ts:355-356`), not inside Keating's own CLI process. So it isn't blocked by stdio inheritance at all — it has direct access to pi's live TUI/renderer objects.

**4. `launchShell` spawn details** (`/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/src/runtime/pi.ts:368-389`): spawns via `spawn(runtime.command, sharedArgs, { cwd, stdio: "inherit", env: {...} })` (binary case) or `spawn(runtime.command, [runtime.cliPath!, ...sharedArgs], { cwd, stdio: "inherit", env })` (non-binary/module case). `stdio: "inherit"` in both branches — full terminal passthrough, no pipe/PTY/Transform anywhere. Confirmed via `grep` of `src/runtime/pi.ts` — no `pty`, `node-pty`, `Transform`, `stdin.pipe`, or `stdout.pipe` present anywhere in `src/runtime/` (only file is `pi.ts`).

**5. `ink` and terminal-formatting libs.** `ink` (`^7.1.0`) is a `package.json` dependency but the only source file importing it is `/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/src/cli/setup.ts` — no other `src/` usage. `package.json` has no `boxen`, `cli-table`/`cli-table3`, `ansi-escapes`, or `terminal-kit` dependencies; `chalk` is only present transitively as a dependency of `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` itself, not a direct Keating dependency.

**Conclusion for approach:** Since the hyperteacher extension already runs inside pi's process with full `ctx.ui` access, option (a) — using pi's native plugin/rendering hooks (`registerMessageRenderer` + `sendMessage`, or richer `details` on `AgentToolResult`) — is available and is the natural fit, not (b) wrapping/parsing pi's inherited stdout from the outside.

Project: "keating" at /home/diogenes/Projects/keating — a teaching agent app with a CLI and a web app (web/). Task: design an implementation plan to bring the CLI/TUI's interactive tool rendering (quiz, ask_user_question, goal, plan/map/verify artifacts) up to parity with the web UI's rich interactive card rendering. Do NOT write code — produce a detailed implementation plan only.

## Established facts from prior investigation (trust these, don't re-derive)

**Architecture**: Keating's CLI (`keating shell`) spawns an external agent runtime binary called `pi` (npm package `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` v0.80.2) via `spawn(..., { stdio: "inherit" })` in `/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/src/runtime/pi.ts` (`launchShell`, lines ~312-389). Keating's own tool logic lives in `/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/src/pi/hyperteacher-extension.ts` (1363 lines), loaded by pi via `--extension <path>` (pi.ts:355-356). Crucially: **this extension code runs INSIDE the pi process**, not inside Keating's own CLI process — so it is NOT blocked by the `stdio:"inherit"` passthrough. It has live access to pi's real TUI/renderer objects via `ExtensionContext.ui`.

**pi's relevant APIs** (from `node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts` and sibling `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core/dist/types.d.ts`):
- `AgentToolResult<T>` shape: `{ content: (TextContent|ImageContent)[]; details: T; terminate?: boolean }` (pi-agent-core/dist/types.d.ts:306-316). `content` is what's sent back to the model (text); `details` is arbitrary structured data explicitly meant "for logs or UI rendering."
- `registerMessageRenderer<T>(customType: string, renderer: MessageRenderer<T>)` where `MessageRenderer<T> = (message: CustomMessage<T>, options, theme) => Component | undefined` (extensions/types.d.ts ~800, 864-867). This lets an extension register a custom terminal UI `Component` (from `@earendil-works/pi-tui`) keyed by a custom message type.
- `sendMessage(...)` — emits a `CustomMessage<T>` that pi's TUI will route to the matching renderer.
- `ExtensionContext.ui` already used extensively in hyperteacher-extension.ts: `ctx.ui.select(title, labels)` (lines 255, 1170, 1271), `ctx.ui.input(title, prefill)` (line 263), `ctx.ui.confirm(title, summary)` (line 329), `ctx.ui.setEditorText(...)`, `ctx.ui.setWidget`/`setHeader` (lines 1346-1349), `ctx.ui.notify`, `ctx.ui.editor`, `ctx.ui.addAutocompleteProvider`.
- `@earendil-works/pi-tui` provides `Component`, `TUI`, `OverlayHandle` primitives — the actual terminal rendering building blocks (need to inspect its type defs / README for what Component authoring looks like — box drawing, lists, selectable items, etc.)

**Current tool behavior (CLI side), all in hyperteacher-extension.ts**:
- `quiz` tool (~line 732-746): returns flat markdown Q&A text via `quizToMarkdown` + an inline answer key string — no structure, no interactivity.
- `ask_user_question` (~line 959-1004): builds payload and embeds `<keating-question json=${JSON.stringify(payload)} />` (single JSON-encoded) as literal text in the result — pi has no parser for this tag today, so it's just printed as raw text to the user. This is clearly meant to mirror the web tag-based approach but was never wired to a CLI renderer.
- `plan`, `map`, `animate`, `verify` — write artifact files and print a path like `[artifact://map]`; no visual rendering in CLI at all today.

**Web side (for behavioral parity — NOT to be copied structurally, since CLI has a completely different rendering substrate)**:
- Web tools in `/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/browser-tools.ts` double-JSON-encode payloads into tags like `<keating-quiz json=... />`, `<keating-question ... />`, `<keating-goal ... />`.
- `/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/components/AssistantChatPanel.tsx` parses these tags (`parseInteractiveSegments`, ~line 1078) and renders React components: `QuizRenderer.tsx`, `QuizResultCard.tsx`, `GoalRenderer.tsx`.
- User interaction on these cards dispatches `window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("keating:question-answered"/"keating:quiz-submitted"/...))`, and `AssistantChatPanel`'s `onNew` listens (lines ~2855-2971) and feeds the answer back into the conversation as a new user message.
- The CLI equivalent of "feed answer back as a new message" should be: the extension's tool handler itself is already in the conversation loop (it's a tool call), so for something like `ask_user_question` the natural mechanism is to just use `ctx.ui.select`/`ctx.ui.input` synchronously inside the tool handler and return the user's answer directly as the tool result content — no round-trip through a "new message" needed, since pi tools can block for interactive input already (this is simpler than the web's event-based flow, not a limitation).
- Quiz is post-lesson, agent-authored (no templates) per project conventions — grading also needs a "submit answers, get graded" round trip; on web this is `keating-quiz` (render) → user submits → `keating-quiz-result`/`keating-quiz-grade` (a follow-up tool call re-invokes the agent to grade). The CLI needs an equivalent: collect answers via interactive prompts, then likely call back into the model (or a `grade_quiz` tool) with those answers.
- Named tag types the web project already conventionally uses: `keating-quiz`, `keating-scene`, `keating-question`, `keating-goal`, `keating-quiz-result`, `keating-quiz-grade`.

**Project conventions to respect** (from CLAUDE.md/memory, do not violate in the plan):
- No templates/fallback rendering — quiz/plan/map/verify content must be agent-authored; don't invent template-based rendering that bypasses agent authorship.
- Use bun (not pnpm/npm) for scripts.
- Tool schemas are currently NOT shared between CLI and web (each defines its own tool set independently) — flag this as a pre-existing gap; note whether unifying schemas is in-scope or should be a separate follow-up (lean towards: out of scope for this task, unless trivially easy).

## What I need from you

1. Inspect `@earendil-works/pi-tui`'s type definitions/README (in node_modules) to understand what a custom `Component` looks like in practice — box drawing, focus/selection, keyboard input handling — so the plan's renderer designs are concrete and buildable, not hand-wavy.
2. Inspect the full `registerMessageRenderer` / `CustomMessage` / `sendMessage` API surface and any example usage in pi's own dist or docs (or existing Keating code, if any already uses it — grep hyperteacher-extension.ts and elsewhere in src/ for `registerMessageRenderer`, `sendMessage`, `CustomMessage`).
3. Design concrete Component-based renderers for: (a) quiz (question list + answer collection + grading round trip), (b) ask_user_question (likely can just use existing `ctx.ui.select`/`ctx.ui.input` — confirm and specify exactly how, since it may need no new Component at all), (c) goal tracking, (d) plan/map/verify artifact previews (at minimum a nicely formatted box/summary in the terminal, since these are file artifacts).
4. Specify the exact code touch points: which functions in hyperteacher-extension.ts change, what new files (if any) get added under src/pi/ or src/cli/, and how `AgentToolResult.details` + `registerMessageRenderer` fit together for tools that need rich rendering (quiz, goal) vs. tools that can just use `ctx.ui` synchronous prompts (ask_user_question).
5. Address the quiz grading round-trip concretely: what triggers grading (a follow-up tool call from the agent, e.g. a `grade_quiz` tool mirroring web's `keating-quiz-grade`?), and how the CLI collects answers before that.
6. Note any risks/unknowns (e.g. whether `registerMessageRenderer`'s Component API can express what's needed, whether pi's TUI supports scrollable/multi-line rich content, version constraints on pi v0.80.2).

Produce a structured implementation plan (not code) with concrete file paths and function-level touch points, suitable for a senior engineer to execute. Keep it focused and avoid scope creep beyond CLI/TUI rendering parity for quiz, ask_user_question, goal, and plan/map/verify artifact previews.

# Implementation Plan: CLI/TUI Interactive Tool Rendering Parity

## Summary of investigation

The key discovery that reframes this task: pi's extension API (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` v0.80.2, TypeBox schema, dist type defs at `node_modules/.bun/@earendil-works+pi-coding-agent@0.80.2+.../dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts`) exposes **two separate, purpose-built mechanisms**, and the right one differs per tool:

1. **`ToolDefinition.renderCall` / `renderResult`** (types.d.ts ~L333-364) — per-tool custom rendering hooks:
   ```
   renderCall?: (args, theme, context: ToolRenderContext) => Component
   renderResult?: (result: AgentToolResult<TDetails>, options: ToolRenderResultOptions, theme, context: ToolRenderContext) => Component
   ```
   `ToolRenderContext` gives `state` (persistent per-tool-row state), `invalidate()` (request redraw), `toolCallId`, `expanded`, `isPartial`, etc. This is the **direct analog of the web's tag-parsing + React-component rendering** — `details` on `AgentToolResult` is exactly the payload a `renderResult` closure receives, so quiz/plan/map/verify/goal tool results can render rich `Component` trees keyed off `result.details` without any text-tag parsing at all. **hyperteacher-extension.ts currently never sets `renderCall`/`renderResult` on any tool** (confirmed via grep — only `execute` is implemented, via the `keatingToolMaker` helper at line 646).

2. **`ExtensionContext.ui.custom<T>(factory, options)`** (types.d.ts ~L116-126) — shows a focused, optionally-overlaid `Component` and resolves a promise when the user finishes interacting with it (`done(result)` callback). This is the mechanism for a tool's `execute()` to **block synchronously on rich interactive input** (multi-question forms, matching/classification tables) — exactly what `ask_user_question` needs, and richer than the existing `ctx.ui.select/input/confirm` primitives already used elsewhere in the file (lines 255, 263, 329, 1170, 1271).

3. `registerMessageRenderer`/`sendMessage`/`CustomMessage` (the API named in the original brief) is a **third, less-fitting mechanism**: it's for extension-injected standalone messages in the transcript (like a system note), not for tool-call results, and requires manually calling `sendMessage` and reconstructing message plumbing. **Recommendation: do not use it for this task.** Tool results already have a native rich-rendering path (`renderResult`) that fits better and requires less new plumbing (no manual message injection, automatically ties to the tool-call's `details`).

4. `Component` (from `@earendil-works/pi-tui`, dist at `node_modules/.bun/@earendil-works+pi-tui@0.80.2/.../dist/tui.d.ts`) is a small interface: `render(width): string[]`, optional `handleInput(data)`, `invalidate()`. Ready-made building blocks exist and should be reused/composed rather than hand-rolling ANSI: `Box` (padding/background container), `Markdown` (full markdown-to-ANSI renderer with theme, code blocks, tables), `SelectList` (arrow-key selectable list with descriptions — ideal for MCQ/goal-step-cycling), `Container` (composes children). These live in `@earendil-works/pi-tui/dist/components/*.d.ts` and are exported from the package's `index.d.ts`.

## Architectural decision per tool

| Tool | Mechanism | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `ask_user_question` | `ctx.ui.custom()` (or, for simple choice-only cases, existing `ctx.ui.select`/`ctx.ui.input`) called synchronously inside `execute()`; answer returned directly as tool result content | Tool calls in pi can block; no round-trip through "new message" needed (unlike web, which has no way to pause a tool call, hence its event+re-message hack). This is *simpler* than web's flow, not a gap. |
| `quiz` | `renderResult` on the `quiz` tool for the display; a **new `ctx.ui.custom()` call inside `execute()`** (or a dedicated overlay Component) to collect answers before returning; a **new `grade_quiz` tool** (mirroring web's) for the open-ended grading round trip, also with a `renderResult` to show updated grades | Quiz must stay agent-authored (no templates) — CLI reuses `generateQuiz`/`Quiz` type from `src/core/quiz.ts` unchanged; only the *collection/rendering* layer is new. |
| `set_learner_goal` / `list_learner_goals` / `update_goal_step` | New tools (don't exist in CLI today) + `renderResult` with a `SelectList`-based cycling Component mirroring `GoalRenderer.tsx`'s "tap step to advance status" UX, adapted to arrow-keys+enter | Confirmed via grep: **no goal tooling exists in `hyperteacher-extension.ts` at all today** — this is a bigger gap than "just rendering," it needs the tool layer added too. |

1. **`ToolDefinition.renderCall` / `renderResult`** (types.d.ts ~L333-364) — per-tool custom rendering hooks:
   ```
   renderCall?: (args, theme, context: ToolRenderContext) => Component
   renderResult?: (result: AgentToolResult<TDetails>, options: ToolRenderResultOptions, theme, context: ToolRenderContext) => Component
   ```
   `ToolRenderContext` gives `state` (persistent per-tool-row state), `invalidate()` (request redraw), `toolCallId`, `expanded`, `isPartial`, etc. This is the **direct analog of the web's tag-parsing + React-component rendering** — `details` on `AgentToolResult` is exactly the payload a `renderResult` closure receives, so quiz/plan/map/verify/goal tool results can render rich `Component` trees keyed off `result.details` without any text-tag parsing at all. **hyperteacher-extension.ts currently never sets `renderCall`/`renderResult` on any tool** (confirmed via grep — only `execute` is implemented, via the `keatingToolMaker` helper at line 646).

- Auto-grade objective types (`multiple_choice`, `true_false`, `fill_in` where `correctAnswer` is a literal match) against `quiz.answerKey` locally, exactly like the web's client-side grading — this needs porting a small comparison utility, not duplicating web's full grading logic since CLI's `QuestionType` union is simpler (no `multi_select`/`slider`/`dropdown` — confirmed by reading `src/core/quiz.ts` lines 8-19).
- For open-ended types (`short_answer`, `transfer`), do **not** grade locally. Return a tool result whose `details` includes `{ resultId, objectiveScore, openEndedQuestions: [...] }` and whose `content` text explicitly instructs the model to call the new `grade_quiz` tool with `result_id` and per-question verdicts — this mirrors the web's exact mechanism (confirmed at `web/src/components/AssistantChatPanel.tsx` ~L2930: `` `Grade the open-ended answers... by calling the grade_quiz tool with result_id "${resultId}"...` ``). The CLI doesn't need an event/message round-trip like the web (no DOM to dispatch from) — the returned tool-result *content text itself* is what nudges the agent's next turn to invoke `grade_quiz`, which is the normal tool-calling mechanism.
- Add new tool `grade_quiz` (mirrors `web/src/keating/browser-tools.ts` L1176-1216 exactly in parameter shape: `result_id: string`, `grades: [{question_id, verdict, note?}]`), storing results in-memory keyed by `resultId` (module-level `Map`, matching how `speechToolRegistrations`/`keatingToolRegistrations` already use `WeakSet`s scoped to the `pi` instance at the top of the file) so a later `renderResult` for the *original* quiz tool call can be invalidated/updated — this requires either (a) storing a reference to the `ToolRenderContext.invalidate` callback from the quiz's `renderResult` so `grade_quiz`'s execute can call it, or (b) simpler: `grade_quiz`'s own `renderResult` renders the updated grade summary as its own card (like web's separate `QuizResultCard`), avoiding cross-tool-call mutation entirely. **Recommend (b)** — much less coupling, matches web's actual architecture (`keating-quiz-result` and `keating-quiz-grade` are two separate rendered artifacts, not a mutated single card).

### 5. Goals (net-new tool surface, ~176 lines to port from `web/src/keating/goals.ts`)

Web's `buildGoal`, `advanceGoalStep`, `computeGoalProgress`, and the `LearnerGoal`/`GoalStep`/`GoalStepStatus` types (`web/src/keating/goals.ts`) have no CLI counterpart at all — confirmed via `find src -iname "*goal*"` returning nothing.
- Add `src/core/goals.ts` — port the pure functions/types (they appear to be storage-agnostic based on `GoalRenderer.tsx`'s usage).
- Add persistence: goals need a durable store analogous to `src/core/learner-state.ts` (`loadLearnerState`/`saveLearnerState` pattern) — e.g. `src/core/goal-state.ts` with `loadGoals(cwd)`/`saveGoal(cwd, goal)`, writing JSON under the same project-scaffold directory used by `learnerStatePath` (`src/core/paths.ts`).
- Add three tools to `hyperteacher-extension.ts`, mirroring `web/src/keating/browser-tools.ts` L1704-1805 (`set_learner_goal`, `list_learner_goals`, `update_goal_step`), using `keatingToolMaker` plus a `renderResult` that shows a `SelectList`/`Box` goal-progress card (steps with status glyphs, progress bar as a simple `[####----] 4/10` bar since terminal has no CSS width tricks) — closely mirroring `GoalRenderer.tsx`'s layout (title, description, progress, ordered steps with kind labels and "Next" tag) but rendered as static text/box rather than a click-to-advance UI (advancing is done via `update_goal_step`, a normal tool call the agent makes on learner request — the CLI doesn't need a clickable card since there's no mouse-driven advance flow expected in terminal use, only agent-driven).

### 6. Tool-schema duplication (flag only, out of scope)

Confirmed: CLI (`hyperteacher-extension.ts`, plain JSON-schema-shaped objects cast `as any`) and web (`browser-tools.ts`, its own `createTool` wrapper) define tool schemas completely independently already, for all existing tools. Porting goal/grade_quiz tools will add to this duplication but not create a new category of problem. Recommend **treating unification as an explicit follow-up**, not in this task's scope — the two runtimes have different type systems (TypeBox vs. plain object) and doing it well is a separate refactor.

## Risks / unknowns

- **No built-in scrolling/pagination primitive**: `Markdown`/`Box`/`SelectList` render everything into `width`-bounded lines with no viewport clipping of their own — `TUI`/overlay handles the terminal viewport, but a long quiz (10+ questions) rendered as one `Component` may exceed screen height. Needs verification against `ctx.ui.custom`'s `overlayOptions` (`maxHeight` is supported per `OverlayOptions` in `tui.d.ts` L76-103) — likely fine if the quiz session is paginated one-question-per-`ctx.ui.custom()`-call rather than rendered as a single giant Component; confirm this UX choice before implementing an all-at-once form.
- **`AnswerFormComponent` for classification/matching questions** is the most complex new Component (table-like row-cursor UI); `SelectList` doesn't natively support 2D grid navigation, so this needs bespoke `handleInput` cursor logic — budget real design/dev time here, it's the single largest risk item.
- **pi v0.80.2 is a moving external dependency** (`node_modules/.bun/@earendil-works+pi-coding-agent@0.80.2...`) — `renderCall`/`renderResult`/`ui.custom` are all present in this version's `.d.ts`, so no blocking version risk found, but pin/verify behavior against the actual installed `.js` (not just `.d.ts`) since dist types can lag runtime in some pre-1.0 packages — worth a quick smoke test (`ctx.ui.custom` resolving/rendering) very early, before committing to the full quiz/goal design.
- **`grade_quiz`'s in-memory `resultId` store** is process-lifetime only (lost on CLI restart) — acceptable for a single interactive session (matches web's session-scoped behavior) but should be documented, not silently assumed.

# CLI/TUI Interactive Tool Rendering Parity

## Context

Keating's web UI renders tool results (quiz, ask_user_question, goals, plan/map/verify artifacts) as rich interactive React cards (`QuizRenderer.tsx`, `GoalRenderer.tsx`, etc.), parsed from double-JSON-encoded tags and wired back to the agent via `window` events. The CLI (`keating shell`) has no equivalent: it spawns an external `pi` binary (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` v0.80.2) with `stdio: "inherit"`, and Keating's tools (defined in `src/pi/hyperteacher-extension.ts`, loaded into `pi` as an extension) just return flat markdown/text. `ask_user_question` even embeds a `<keating-question json=... />` tag that nothing in the CLI parses — dead output. Goal tracking (`set_learner_goal`/`list_learner_goals`/`update_goal_step`) doesn't exist in the CLI at all.

Investigation found that because the extension runs **inside** the `pi` process (not blocked by `stdio: inherit`), pi's own extension API already provides native, purpose-built rendering hooks — no stdout-wrapping/parsing hack needed:
- `ToolDefinition.renderResult(result, options, theme, context) => Component` — renders a tool's `AgentToolResult.details` as a live terminal `Component`. Direct analog of the web's tag→React-component path.
- `ExtensionContext.ui.custom<T>(factory, options) => Promise<T>` — shows a focused/overlaid `Component` and resolves when the user finishes interacting. Already used elsewhere in the file via the simpler `ctx.ui.select/input/confirm` (lines 255, 263, 329, 1170, 1271).
- `@earendil-works/pi-tui` ships ready-made components: `Box`, `Markdown`, `SelectList`, `Input`, `Container`, `Text` — enough to compose everything needed without hand-rolled ANSI.

All of this was confirmed directly against the installed `.d.ts` files (not just the plan's claims), so the approach is verified, not speculative.

**Decisions confirmed with the user:**
- `ask_user_question` will **block synchronously** via `ctx.ui.custom()` and return the answer directly as the tool result — a genuine UX improvement over today's "print a tag, wait for the learner's next raw chat message" flow.
- Quiz answers are collected as a **single combined form** (not paginated per-question); overflow risk on very long quizzes is accepted and can be revisited later if it's a real problem.
- Goal tracking tools are **in scope** — full parity with web, including net-new tool registration and persistence, not just rendering.

## Approach

### 1. Shared TUI building blocks — new file `src/pi/tui-components.ts`

Reusable helpers built on `@earendil-works/pi-tui` primitives (avoid bloating the already-1363-line `hyperteacher-extension.ts` further):
- `renderArtifactPreview(theme, title, markdownContent)` → `Box` + `Markdown`, used by plan/map/animate/verify `renderResult`s.
- `renderQuizCard(theme, quiz, state)` → question list with per-question status glyphs (unanswered/answered/graded), used by quiz's `renderResult` in both pre- and post-grading states.
- `renderGoalCard(theme, goal)` → title/description/progress bar (`[####----] 4/10`) + ordered steps with status glyphs and a "Next" marker, mirroring `GoalRenderer.tsx`'s layout as static text (no click-to-advance; advancing happens via the `update_goal_step` tool call).
- `AnswerFormComponent` (implements `Component`) — the one genuinely new nontrivial component. Composes `SelectList` for choice-type questions, `Input` for free text/fill-in, and bespoke `handleInput` cursor logic for classification/matching (2D-ish row navigation; `SelectList` doesn't natively support this). Used by both `ask_user_question` and quiz answer collection.

### 2. `keatingToolMaker` — extend to accept render hooks (`src/pi/hyperteacher-extension.ts` ~line 646)

Extend the helper's signature with an optional `render?: { result?: (result, options, theme, context) => Component }` param, threaded into the tool object literal alongside the existing `execute`. Every artifact tool (`plan`, `map`, `animate`, `verify`) already returns `{ content, details: artifact }` (lines ~684-751) with the artifact path in `details` — so adding a preview is just wiring a `renderResult` that reads that path and calls `renderArtifactPreview`, no change to `execute()` bodies.

### 3. `ask_user_question` (~lines 958-1007)

- Inside `execute()`, call `ctx.ui.custom<Answer>(factory, { overlay: true })`, where `factory` builds an `AnswerFormComponent` seeded from the question/choices/items/type/hint params, resolving via `done(answer)`.
- Return the resolved answer as `content: [{ type: "text", text: <readable summary> }]`, `details: { question, answer }`.
- Remove the now-dead `<keating-question json=... />` tag construction.
- Guard on `ctx.mode === "tui"` (`ExtensionMode = "tui" | "rpc" | "json" | "print"`) with a fallback to today's plain-text behavior for non-interactive modes, so headless/RPC usage doesn't break.

### 4. Quiz (~lines 935-957) + new `grade_quiz` tool

- Keep `generateQuiz`/`quizToMarkdown`/`Quiz` types from `src/core/quiz.ts` as the sole content source — no template rendering, per project convention ([[project_no_templates_authored_artifacts]]).
- `execute()`: after generating the quiz, call `ctx.ui.custom()` with a combined-form `AnswerFormComponent` listing all questions, collecting all answers in one pass.
- Auto-grade objective types (`multiple_choice`, `true_false`, literal-match `fill_in`) locally against `quiz.answerKey` (port a small comparison helper — CLI's `QuestionType` union is simpler than web's, no `multi_select`/`slider`/`dropdown`).
- For open-ended types (`short_answer`, `transfer`), don't grade locally. Return `details: { resultId, objectiveScore, openEndedQuestions }` and `content` text that instructs the model to call `grade_quiz` next — mirroring `web/src/keating/browser-tools.ts` L1176-1216 exactly in parameter shape (`result_id`, `grades: [{question_id, verdict, note?}]`). No event/message round-trip needed (unlike web) — the tool result's own text nudges the agent's next turn.
- `grade_quiz` renders its **own** result card (separate from the quiz card, matching web's `keating-quiz-result`/`keating-quiz-grade` being separate artifacts) rather than mutating the original quiz's rendered `Component` — avoids cross-tool-call state coupling.
- Store pending `resultId → quiz/answers` in a module-level `Map` (process-lifetime only, matching how other per-session state is scoped at the top of the file) — acceptable since this mirrors the web's session-scoped grading state.

### 5. Goal tracking — net new (~176 lines to port from `web/src/keating/goals.ts`)

- Add `src/core/goals.ts`: port `LearnerGoal`/`GoalStep`/`GoalStepStatus` types and the pure functions `buildGoal`, `advanceGoalStep`, `computeGoalProgress` unchanged.
- Add `src/core/goal-state.ts`: `loadGoals(cwd)`/`saveGoal(cwd, goal)`, following the existing `loadLearnerState`/`saveLearnerState` pattern (`src/core/learner-state.ts`), storing JSON under the same project-scaffold directory as `learnerStatePath` (`src/core/paths.ts`).
- Add three tools to `hyperteacher-extension.ts` via `keatingToolMaker`, mirroring `web/src/keating/browser-tools.ts` L1704-1805 (`set_learner_goal`, `list_learner_goals`, `update_goal_step`), each with a `renderResult` using `renderGoalCard`.

### 6. Out of scope (flagged, not addressed here)

- Unifying tool schemas between CLI (plain JSON-schema objects) and web (TypeBox-free `createTool` wrapper) — pre-existing duplication, adding goal/grade_quiz tools continues the existing pattern rather than creating a new problem. Real unification is a separate refactor (different type systems).

## Critical files

- `src/pi/hyperteacher-extension.ts` — main edits (keatingToolMaker, ask_user_question, quiz, +grade_quiz, +3 goal tools)
- `src/pi/tui-components.ts` — **new**, shared render helpers + `AnswerFormComponent`
- `src/core/quiz.ts` — read only, reused as-is
- `src/core/goals.ts` — **new**, ported pure logic from `web/src/keating/goals.ts`
- `src/core/goal-state.ts` — **new**, persistence following `src/core/learner-state.ts` pattern
- `src/core/paths.ts` — reused for storage path conventions
- Reference only (not edited): `web/src/keating/browser-tools.ts` (L1175-1217, L1704-1805), `web/src/keating/goals.ts`, `web/src/components/GoalRenderer.tsx`, `web/src/components/QuizRenderer.tsx`
- pi API reference (not edited): `node_modules/.bun/@earendil-works+pi-coding-agent@0.80.2+68e5448f0edf20e3/.../dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts`, `node_modules/.bun/@earendil-works+pi-tui@0.80.2/.../dist/index.d.ts`

## Risks

- `AnswerFormComponent`'s classification/matching cursor logic is the largest net-new UI complexity (no existing `SelectList` support for 2D grid nav).
- No built-in scrolling in `Box`/`Markdown`/`SelectList` — accepted risk for single-combined-form quizzes per user decision; revisit with pagination later if long quizzes overflow the terminal in practice.
- `pi` is a pre-1.0 external dependency; do an early smoke test of `ctx.ui.custom()` + `renderResult` wiring (e.g. on the simplest artifact tool) before investing in the full quiz/goal build-out, in case runtime behavior diverges from the `.d.ts`.

## Verification

1. `bun run typecheck` (or repo's equivalent) after each major section to catch API-shape drift early against pi's types.
2. Manually run `keating shell` in a real terminal (not piped) and exercise:
   - `ask_user_question` with each type (choice, text, blanks, classification, matching) — confirm the form renders, blocks, and the answer is returned correctly.
   - `quiz` → answer mixed objective + open-ended questions → confirm auto-grading + the follow-up `grade_quiz` call renders a separate result card.
   - `plan`/`map`/`verify` → confirm artifact preview renders instead of a bare `[artifact://...]` line.
   - `set_learner_goal` → `list_learner_goals` → `update_goal_step` → confirm goal card renders and persists across a new `keating shell` session in the same project.
3. Confirm non-interactive mode (`rpc`/`print`, if reachable via existing CLI flags) still returns plain-text fallback for `ask_user_question` without hanging.

# CLI/TUI Interactive Tool Rendering Parity

## Context

Keating's web UI renders tool results (quiz, ask_user_question, goals, plan/map/verify artifacts) as rich interactive React cards (`QuizRenderer.tsx`, `GoalRenderer.tsx`, etc.), parsed from double-JSON-encoded tags and wired back to the agent via `window` events. The CLI (`keating shell`) has no equivalent: it spawns an external `pi` binary (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` v0.80.2) with `stdio: "inherit"`, and Keating's tools (defined in `src/pi/hyperteacher-extension.ts`, loaded into `pi` as an extension) just return flat markdown/text. `ask_user_question` even embeds a `<keating-question json=... />` tag that nothing in the CLI parses — dead output. Goal tracking (`set_learner_goal`/`list_learner_goals`/`update_goal_step`) doesn't exist in the CLI at all.

Investigation found that because the extension runs **inside** the `pi` process (not blocked by `stdio: inherit`), pi's own extension API already provides native, purpose-built rendering hooks — no stdout-wrapping/parsing hack needed:
- `ToolDefinition.renderResult(result, options, theme, context) => Component` — renders a tool's `AgentToolResult.details` as a live terminal `Component`. Direct analog of the web's tag→React-component path.
- `ExtensionContext.ui.custom<T>(factory, options) => Promise<T>` — shows a focused/overlaid `Component` and resolves when the user finishes interacting. Already used elsewhere in the file via the simpler `ctx.ui.select/input/confirm` (lines 255, 263, 329, 1170, 1271).
- `@earendil-works/pi-tui` ships ready-made components: `Box`, `Markdown`, `SelectList`, `Input`, `Container`, `Text` — enough to compose everything needed without hand-rolled ANSI.

All of this was confirmed directly against the installed `.d.ts` files (not just the plan's claims), so the approach is verified, not speculative.

**Decisions confirmed with the user:**
- `ask_user_question` will **block synchronously** via `ctx.ui.custom()` and return the answer directly as the tool result — a genuine UX improvement over today's "print a tag, wait for the learner's next raw chat message" flow.
- Quiz answers are collected as a **single combined form** (not paginated per-question); overflow risk on very long quizzes is accepted and can be revisited later if it's a real problem.
- Goal tracking tools are **in scope** — full parity with web, including net-new tool registration and persistence, not just rendering.

## Approach

### 1. Shared TUI building blocks — new file `src/pi/tui-components.ts`

Reusable helpers built on `@earendil-works/pi-tui` primitives (avoid bloating the already-1363-line `hyperteacher-extension.ts` further):
- `renderArtifactPreview(theme, title, markdownContent)` → `Box` + `Markdown`, used by plan/map/animate/verify `renderResult`s.
- `renderQuizCard(theme, quiz, state)` → question list with per-question status glyphs (unanswered/answered/graded), used by quiz's `renderResult` in both pre- and post-grading states.
- `renderGoalCard(theme, goal)` → title/description/progress bar (`[####----] 4/10`) + ordered steps with status glyphs and a "Next" marker, mirroring `GoalRenderer.tsx`'s layout as static text (no click-to-advance; advancing happens via the `update_goal_step` tool call).
- `AnswerFormComponent` (implements `Component`) — the one genuinely new nontrivial component. Composes `SelectList` for choice-type questions, `Input` for free text/fill-in, and bespoke `handleInput` cursor logic for classification/matching (2D-ish row navigation; `SelectList` doesn't natively support this). Used by both `ask_user_question` and quiz answer collection.

### 2. `keatingToolMaker` — extend to accept render hooks (`src/pi/hyperteacher-extension.ts` ~line 646)

Extend the helper's signature with an optional `render?: { result?: (result, options, theme, context) => Component }` param, threaded into the tool object literal alongside the existing `execute`. Every artifact tool (`plan`, `map`, `animate`, `verify`) already returns `{ content, details: artifact }` (lines ~684-751) with the artifact path in `details` — so adding a preview is just wiring a `renderResult` that reads that path and calls `renderArtifactPreview`, no change to `execute()` bodies.

### 3. `ask_user_question` (~lines 958-1007)

- Inside `execute()`, call `ctx.ui.custom<Answer>(factory, { overlay: true })`, where `factory` builds an `AnswerFormComponent` seeded from the question/choices/items/type/hint params, resolving via `done(answer)`.
- Return the resolved answer as `content: [{ type: "text", text: <readable summary> }]`, `details: { question, answer }`.
- Remove the now-dead `<keating-question json=... />` tag construction.
- Guard on `ctx.mode === "tui"` (`ExtensionMode = "tui" | "rpc" | "json" | "print"`) with a fallback to today's plain-text behavior for non-interactive modes, so headless/RPC usage doesn't break.

### 4. Quiz (~lines 935-957) + new `grade_quiz` tool

- Keep `generateQuiz`/`quizToMarkdown`/`Quiz` types from `src/core/quiz.ts` as the sole content source — no template rendering, per project convention ([[project_no_templates_authored_artifacts]]).
- `execute()`: after generating the quiz, call `ctx.ui.custom()` with a combined-form `AnswerFormComponent` listing all questions, collecting all answers in one pass.
- Auto-grade objective types (`multiple_choice`, `true_false`, literal-match `fill_in`) locally against `quiz.answerKey` (port a small comparison helper — CLI's `QuestionType` union is simpler than web's, no `multi_select`/`slider`/`dropdown`).
- For open-ended types (`short_answer`, `transfer`), don't grade locally. Return `details: { resultId, objectiveScore, openEndedQuestions }` and `content` text that instructs the model to call `grade_quiz` next — mirroring `web/src/keating/browser-tools.ts` L1176-1216 exactly in parameter shape (`result_id`, `grades: [{question_id, verdict, note?}]`). No event/message round-trip needed (unlike web) — the tool result's own text nudges the agent's next turn.
- `grade_quiz` renders its **own** result card (separate from the quiz card, matching web's `keating-quiz-result`/`keating-quiz-grade` being separate artifacts) rather than mutating the original quiz's rendered `Component` — avoids cross-tool-call state coupling.
- Store pending `resultId → quiz/answers` in a module-level `Map` (process-lifetime only, matching how other per-session state is scoped at the top of the file) — acceptable since this mirrors the web's session-scoped grading state.

### 5. Goal tracking — net new (~176 lines to port from `web/src/keating/goals.ts`)

- Add `src/core/goals.ts`: port `LearnerGoal`/`GoalStep`/`GoalStepStatus` types and the pure functions `buildGoal`, `advanceGoalStep`, `computeGoalProgress` unchanged.

### 6. Out of scope (flagged, not addressed here)

- Unifying tool schemas between CLI (plain JSON-schema objects) and web (TypeBox-free `createTool` wrapper) — pre-existing duplication, adding goal/grade_quiz tools continues the existing pattern rather than creating a new problem. Real unification is a separate refactor (different type systems).

## Critical files

# Split up src/pi/hyperteacher-extension.ts

## Context

`hyperteacher-extension.ts` has grown to ~1650 lines (it was 1363 before this session's CLI-rendering-parity work added the Goals tools, quiz collection/grading, and render hooks). It mixes several genuinely separate concerns in one file: pure text/ANSI formatting helpers, a header/greeting widget, an interactive setup wizard, a `/packages` command, ~24 LLM tool definitions grouped by theme, a speech tool, and the top-level `hyperteacher(pi)` extension entry point that wires up ~21 slash commands and session event handlers. This makes the file slow to navigate and risks merge conflicts as more tools get added. The goal is a mechanical extraction into theme-based modules — no behavior change, same runtime registration order, same exports consumed by `src/runtime/pi.ts` (which only imports the default export).

Confirmed via grep that this is a clean decomposition: each helper group's call sites are either fully contained within one section or shared across exactly two well-understood spots (documented below), so no hidden coupling surprises are expected.

## Target structure

```
src/pi/
  hyperteacher-extension.ts   (slimmed to ~350 lines: default export hyperteacher(pi), topicFromArgs, module state, composition calls)
  ui-helpers.ts               NEW — info(ctx, message)
  text-format.ts              NEW — ANSI_RE, visibleWidth, truncateVisible, padVisible, truncatePlain, centerPlain, wrapWords
  header-component.ts         NEW — createKeatingHeaderComponent + formatHeaderPath/getCurrentModelLabel/getSessionLabel/summarizeLastActivity
  setup-wizard.ts             NEW — SetupChoice, SETUP_* consts, choiceDisplay, selectSetupChoice, inputSetupValue, runKeatingSetupInTui
  commands/
    packages.ts               NEW — packageListText, runPiPackagesCommand
  tools/
    shared.ts                 NEW — keatingToolMaker, artifactPreviewRenderer, getCwd()/setActiveCtx(), PendingQuizResult + pendingQuizResults, feedbackOnlyTopics
    teaching.ts                NEW — plan, map, animate, verify, quiz, grade_quiz
    self-evaluation.ts         NEW — bench, timeline, due, learner_state, trace, policy, outputs
    self-evolution.ts          NEW — auto_improve, evolve, improve, prompt_evolve, prompt_eval
    feedback.ts                 NEW — feedback
    goals.ts                    NEW — set_learner_goal, list_learner_goals, update_goal_step
    ask-user-question.ts        NEW — ask_user_question
    speech.ts                   NEW — voiceToolParameters, registerSpeechTool (+ its own WeakSet guard)
    index.ts                    NEW — registerKeatingTools(pi): imports each category array, WeakSet dedup guard, pi.registerTool loop
  tui-components.ts            (existing, unchanged)
```

Every tool-category file exports a plain array of tool objects (`export const teachingTools = [keatingToolMaker(...), ...]`), matching the shape already built by `keatingToolMaker`. `tools/index.ts` concatenates them and does exactly what `registerKeatingTools` does today (dedup guard + `pi.registerTool` loop) — this preserves registration order exactly.

## Confirmed boundaries (grepped, not guessed)

## Target structure

```
src/pi/
  hyper-teacher/
    index.ts                  was hyperteacher-extension.ts: default export hyperteacher(pi), topicFromArgs, module state, composition calls (~350 lines)

      self-evolution.ts        NEW — auto_improve, evolve, improve, prompt_evolve, prompt_eval
      feedback.ts                NEW — feedback
      goals.ts                   NEW — set_learner_goal, list_learner_goals, update_goal_step
      ask-user-question.ts       NEW — ask_user_question
      speech.ts                  NEW — voiceToolParameters, registerSpeechTool (+ its own WeakSet guard)
      index.ts                   NEW — registerKeatingTools(pi): imports each category array, WeakSet dedup guard, pi.registerTool loop

## Build output path — the one non-mechanical touch point

`src/runtime/pi.ts` (`launchShell`) resolves the *compiled* extension by a hardcoded path (`src/runtime/pi.ts:326-328`):
```ts
const extensionPath = isDist

## Confirmed boundaries (grepped, not guessed)

- **Text helpers** (`ANSI_RE`, `visibleWidth`, `truncateVisible`, `padVisible`, `truncatePlain`, `centerPlain`, `wrapWords`): every call site is inside `createKeatingHeaderComponent` — move together into `header-component.ts`, importing from `text-format.ts`.
- **`info(ctx, message)`**: called inside the setup wizard, ~40 times across `hyper-teacher/index.ts`'s command handlers, and from `commands/packages.ts`. Genuinely shared → its own tiny `ui-helpers.ts` so `setup-wizard.ts` and `commands/packages.ts` don't need to import back from `index.ts` (would create a cycle).
- **`packageListText` / `runPiPackagesCommand`**: self-contained pair, only reachable via the `/packages` command → `commands/packages.ts`.
- **Setup wizard** (`SetupChoice`, `SETUP_PROVIDERS`/`SETUP_MODELS_BY_PROVIDER`/`SETUP_THINKING`/`SETUP_RUNTIMES`, `choiceDisplay`, `selectSetupChoice`, `inputSetupValue`, `runKeatingSetupInTui`): self-contained, only reachable via `/setup` → `setup-wizard.ts`.
- **`feedbackOnlyTopics`**: called from the `learner_state` tool (→ `tools/self-evaluation.ts`) *and* the `/learner-state` command handler in `index.ts` → belongs in `tools/shared.ts`.
- **`getCwd()`**: reads module-level `activeCtx`, set exactly once in the `session_start` event handler. Moving `getCwd` into `tools/shared.ts` means that assignment becomes an exported `setActiveCtx(ctx)` call from `index.ts`, not a direct module-local assignment.
- **`pendingQuizResults` / `PendingQuizResult`**: read/written only by `quiz` and `grade_quiz` (both in `tools/teaching.ts`) → lives in `tools/shared.ts` alongside `keatingToolMaker`.
- **`registerSpeechTool` / `voiceToolParameters` / `speechToolRegistrations`**: fully self-contained (own WeakSet guard, own tool def), called once from composition → `tools/speech.ts`.
- **`topicFromArgs`**: only used inside `index.ts`'s command handlers (12 call sites) → stays in `index.ts`, not worth its own module.
- **`pick`/`up`/`down`/`confused`**: used by the `feedback` tool, the `learner_state` tool (self-evaluation.ts), and the `improve` tool's `pick(...)` call (self-evolution.ts) → `tools/shared.ts`.

## What stays in `hyper-teacher/index.ts`

- `export default function hyperteacher(pi)` — all `pi.registerCommand(...)` blocks and `pi.on(...)` event handlers, unchanged in content, now calling into imported functions (`runKeatingSetupInTui`, `runPiPackagesCommand`, `registerKeatingTools`, `registerSpeechTool`, `createKeatingHeaderComponent`, `info`, `topicFromArgs`).
- `topicFromArgs`, module state (`greetingShown` stays here; `activeCtx` moves into `tools/shared.ts` behind `setActiveCtx`/`getCwd`).
- Imports needed only by command registration (`KEATING_ASCII_LOGO`/`KEATING_SUBTITLE_LINES` etc. move to `header-component.ts` instead, since that's their only consumer).

## Verification

1. `bun x tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — zero errors, matching the pre-split baseline from this session.
2. `bun test ./test/*.test.ts` — same pass count as the pre-split baseline (240 pass / 0 fail).
3. `bun run build` (or at least `bun x tsc -p tsconfig.json` to emit) — confirm `dist/src/pi/hyper-teacher/index.js` is produced, then confirm `src/runtime/pi.ts`'s updated path resolves to that file (`existsSync` check it references).
4. Quick structural diff: the concatenated tool array in `tools/index.ts` has the exact same tool names in the exact same order as today's single array — a `grep -n "^ \"" ` name-order check across the new files vs. a saved copy of the old array is sufficient.
5. Re-run the headless verification script from this session (`/tmp/.../scratchpad/verify-tui.ts`) against the new `hyper-teacher/tui-components.ts` path to confirm nothing broke in the move.
